items.title: 9.2 Lewis concept of acids and bases

source_refs.note: Topic 9.2, printed page 191, with Quick Check 9.1 (page 192).

blocks.text: In 1923, G.N. Lewis proposed a generalized definition of acid-base behavior in which acids and bases are identified by their ability to accept or to donate a pair of electrons and form a coordinate covalent bond.

A Lewis acid is any species (molecule or ion) that can accept a pair of electrons, and a Lewis base is any species (molecule or ion) that can donate a pair of electrons. A Lewis acid-base reaction occurs when a base donates a pair of electrons to an acid.
highlight: A Lewis acid is any species (molecule or ion) that can accept a pair of electrons, and a Lewis base is any species (molecule or ion) that can donate a pair of electrons.

blocks.text: In the following reaction, each of two ammonia molecules, Lewis bases, donates a pair of electrons to a positively charged silver ion, the Lewis acid. The sum of charges on the left side is +1, so the acid-base adduct on the right hand side must carry a charge of +1:

blocks.alt: 2 H-N(H)-H with a red lone pair on N, labelled Lewis base, plus Ag+, labelled Lewis acid, arrow to the bracketed ion [H3N→Ag←NH3]+ in which each N gives its pair to Ag through a coordinate arrow, labelled Acid base adduct.
blocks.caption: Reaction of ammonia (Lewis base) with silver ion (Lewis acid) (original drawing after the scheme printed on p191 of the textbook).

blocks.text: The boron atom in boron trifluoride, BF₃, has only six electrons in its valence shell. Since the boron atom has an incomplete octet, it can behave as an electron pair acceptor. As a result, BF₃ is a very good Lewis acid and reacts with many Lewis bases; a fluoride ion is the Lewis base in this reaction, donating one of its lone pairs:

blocks.alt: A fluoride ion with four lone pairs and a minus charge, labelled Lewis base, plus BF3 drawn with B bonded to three F atoms each carrying three lone pairs, labelled Lewis acid, arrow to the bracketed ion [BF4]- in which one F gives a pair to B through a coordinate arrow (F→B), labelled Acid base adduct.
blocks.caption: Reaction of fluoride ion (Lewis base) with boron trifluoride (Lewis acid) (original drawing after the scheme printed on p191 of the textbook).

blocks.text: The negative charge on the adduct is the sum of charges on the left hand side of the equation is -1, the sum of charges on the right hand side must also be -1.

blocks.prompt:
a) Identify the conjugate acid-base pairs in the following reactions:
(i) HCN(g) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + CN⁻(aq)
(ii) CH₃COOH(l) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + CH₃COO⁻(aq)
(iii) H₂S(g) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₃O⁺(aq) + HS⁻(aq)
(iv) HCl(g) + HCO₃⁻(aq) ⇌ H₂CO₃(aq) + Cl⁻(aq)
blocks.explanation:
In each reaction the species that donates a proton is the acid, and what is left after it loses the proton is its conjugate base.
(i) HCN (acid)/CN⁻ (conjugate base); H₂O (base)/H₃O⁺ (conjugate acid).
(ii) CH₃COOH/CH₃COO⁻; H₂O/H₃O⁺.
(iii) H₂S/HS⁻; H₂O/H₃O⁺.
(iv) HCl donates a proton to HCO₃⁻: HCl/Cl⁻; HCO₃⁻ (base)/H₂CO₃ (its conjugate acid).

blocks.prompt:
b) Identify the Lewis acid and Lewis base in the reaction between:
i. SO₃ and O²⁻
ii. HCl and H₂O
iii. BF₃ and NH₃
Also write down the balanced chemical equation for the reaction and explain.
blocks.explanation:
i. SO₃ + O²⁻ → SO₄²⁻: the oxide ion donates an electron pair to S, so O²⁻ is the Lewis base and SO₃ the Lewis acid.
ii. HCl + H₂O → H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻: a lone pair on the O of water bonds to H⁺, so H₂O is the Lewis base and the H⁺ of HCl the Lewis acid.
iii. BF₃ + NH₃ → H₃N→BF₃: the lone pair on N completes the incomplete octet of B, so NH₃ is the Lewis base and BF₃ the Lewis acid.
